label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Dear Mr Ogunleye,

Thank you very much for picking up my bag and taking the trouble to call the number you found in my lab manual. I am sincerely grateful that you did not throw it away, because many people would have done that. You said God sent you to help, and I am still hoping we can settle this matter in that same spirit of kindness.

The bag is my black Jansport bag, which I forgot in a commercial bus travelling from Oshodi to Igando on the evening of Friday, 6 November. I came down at Ikotun. Inside it are my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, I understand that you have asked for ₦40,000, but I honestly cannot afford that amount. I am a first-year Biology student, and with respect, the bag and everything inside it are not even worth that much. I do not mean any insult by saying this; I simply cannot pay what I do not have.

I can offer ₦10,000 from my allowance to cover your transport and show my appreciation. That is genuinely all I can manage, and I will give it to you when I collect the bag. I hope you will kindly accept it.

My BIO 101 practical holds on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m. The lab attendant is very strict, and without my dissecting kit, I will not be allowed into the laboratory. My ID card and glasses are also very important to me, so this situation is causing me serious concern.

Please choose any convenient day and time before Wednesday for me to collect the bag. I can meet you during the daytime at Ikotun Roundabout or at the gate of Ikotun Police Division, whichever is easier for you. I am suggesting these places simply because they are safe, public meeting points for both of us. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me.

Sir, I truly appreciate your initial effort in contacting me, and I hope we can resolve this peacefully. Kindly reply and confirm the day, time and location that suit you, so I can make arrangements immediately.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your Name]  
First-year Biology undergraduate
